title_original: How Does an Artist Know When She’s Done? A Major Marisa Merz Retrospective Turns the Question on Its Head
editorial_title_zh: 艺术家如何知道作品何时算完成？一场大型玛丽莎·梅尔兹回顾展颠覆了这个问题
editorial_excerpt_zh: 都灵三个场馆向“贫穷艺术”唯一的女性代表致敬。

"尽管如此，梅尔兹在进入聚光灯下时依然难以捉摸。值其诞辰百年之际，一场题为“玛丽莎·梅尔兹：时辰之舞”（Marisa Merz: La danza delle ore）的庞大且多声部的回顾展接管了都灵的三家机构。然而，尽管对其跨越五十多年的作品进行了详尽回顾，她依然充满谜团。都灵市立现代和当代艺术画廊（GAM）强调了她对工作室与家庭的重叠处理；梅尔兹基金会（Fondazione Merz）专注于她对材料的实验；里沃利城堡（Castello di Rivoli）则探讨了她对空间的形而上学介入。与此同时，梅尔兹那些难以捉摸的核心主题——透明、蜕变与炼金术——在其中反复出现。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "credit": "ARTnews", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "正如回顾展的标题所示，这组展览并未遵循按时间顺序排列的路线，因为这样做几乎是不可能的。她的生平依然笼罩在神秘之中。以下是她1960年之前生平中已知的事实：她出生于都灵，父亲是菲亚特公司的雇员，她曾学习舞蹈，后来在其他艺术家的工作室里担任模特。甚至在获得艺评界关注后，她也极少为自己的作品命名或标注日期，并且很难让它们尘埃落定。她的第一个也是最知名的装置作品《活的雕塑》（The Living Sculpture，1966年）的标题说明了一切，它内含了她的一种信念，即完成等同于某种死亡。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/04_Marisa-Merz_Senza-titolo-sd.jpg?w=400", "alt": "", "caption": "玛丽莎·梅尔兹无题且无年代作品，鸣谢：梅尔兹基金会", "credit": "ARTnews", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种动荡不安的态度体现在贯穿展出作品的一种临时性特质上。《活的雕塑》是一件触手般的缝制铝质作品，最初幽闭地悬挂在她家中的天花板上，现在则以闪亮的碎片形式悬挂在GAM和里沃利城堡。她自1970年代至2010年代创作的一系列粗矮的黏土头像“Testine（小头像）”，均未经过烧制，有时还保留着从较大黏土块中切出时如砖块般的粗糙棱角。她那些画在纸张、木头和雪花石膏上的抽象面庞扭曲而模糊，仿佛处于运动中；其中一件无题且无年代的石墨面相，在漩涡般眼睛的旋转线条中不断自我重组。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "与她的“贫穷艺术”同仁一样，梅尔兹对固定性感到沮丧，并被那些随着时间推移而形态变化的材料所吸引。或许正因如此，策展人展出的作品可能是未完成的、直接来自工作室的；人们永远不会知道她是否计划继续创作下去。酒店信纸和便利贴上的笔记依然被大头针固定、用胶带粘或用夹子夹在她的素描和绘画上，这些笔记形态各异地描述着她希望捕捉的情感（例如“表现力强且精致”）、引用文学作品（其中一件作品注释了荷尔德林的最后一首诗），或者仅仅是记录尺寸。人们有一种感觉，梅尔兹随时可能带着针、铅笔或画笔归来，从她停下的地方继续创作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/1.jpg?w=400", "alt": "", "caption": "玛丽莎·梅尔兹：《无题》，1968年。", "credit": "ARTnews", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "为了展现一个构思如何能保持不固定、并在后代艺术家接手时得以延续和演变，这些展览安排了梅尔茨与多位当代女性艺术家——包括莱奥诺尔·安图内斯（Leonor Antunes）、特娅·乔尔贾泽（Thea Djordjadze）和米里亚姆·卡恩（Miriam Cahn）——的作品并置，她们的创作与梅尔茨有着相似的共鸣。塔西塔·迪恩（Tacita Dean）受托在梅尔茨的家中及工作室创作了一系列电影和摄影作品。其中包括16毫米双联短片《Via Milano 13》（2026），捕捉了梅尔茨位于都灵波尔塔帕拉佐（Porta Palazzo）市场附近的公寓景象。在缓慢的镜头中，我们看到由厕纸筒和纸巾卷等蜂窝状纸板圆筒拼成的装置；在其丈夫旧工作室的盘旋桌面上排列着一组“Testine”头像；一幅画有蓝发、红唇鲜艳的面容固定在墙上，其倒影在下方玻璃表面上下颠倒地呈现。在都灵当代艺术馆（GAM）和梅尔茨基金会（Fondazione Merz）呈星形散落展出的这组互补摄影作品，同样向我们好奇的目光敞开了梅尔茨的私人世界，在这些作品被移至展厅开阔的空间之前，镜头捕捉到了它们原本在家具和全家福照片之间的实景。这些影像和图片近乎一种侵入，违背了梅尔茨反对摄影捕捉的禁令——当然，除了艺术家缺席这一事实之外，这种缺席在迪恩冥想般的静止镜头中显露无遗。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "走出这组展览，我发现梅尔茨的创作实践比以往更加难以捉摸。我并非遭遇这一难题的首位评论人。1992年，日耳曼诺·切兰特（Germano Celant）在为《艺术论坛》（Artforum）撰写关于她的作品时曾反思道：“就在它被定义的那一刻，它便逃逸了。”如同艺术家本人一样，梅尔茨的作品虚幻无常，随着光影的变幻而变形，在画框边缘模糊不清，从人们的视线中悄然滑落。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Italian artist Marisa Merz (1926–2019) was famously camera-shy. In rare snapshots, such as a captivating photograph taken by Claudio Abate at her 1975 solo show in Rome, she would retreat from the camera’s gaze. Before Abate’s camera, Merz appears clad in her woven nylon Scarpette (Little Shoes) , 1968, her back to him as she gazes out an open window at the moon.

The turn away is emblematic of Merz’s artistic ethos writ large. As she once wrote, in a 1975 issue of Data Arte magazine, “The artist is already an established role, like the wife, the son. But I don’t go along with these roles.”

Merz was the only woman affiliated with Arte Povera , a loose movement christened in 1967 by curator Germano Celant that rejected the commodification of art and celebrated presence and materiality through nontraditional media and process-based practices. Even within this iconoclast milieu, she remained an outlier, not only for her inscription of domestic labor into her work—in her 1967 film The Count , she is seen in her kitchen sorting beans—but also for her use of figuration from the 1970s onward. Her unruly aluminum installations, paraffin pools, and woven forms were overlooked in the 1960s and 1970s, but she has gained wider recognition in recent years. Since the 1990s, major exhibitions of her work have been staged across Europe and the US, and in 2013, the Venice Biennale honored her with a Golden Lion.

Still, Merz remains evasive even as she enters the spotlight. A sprawling and polyphonic retrospective titled “Marisa Merz: La danza delle ore (The Dance of the Hours)” has taken over three Turin institutions on the centenary of her birth. Yet despite its exhaustive review of more than five decades of her work, she remains enigmatic. The Galleria d’Arte Moderna e Contemporanea Torino (GAM) emphasizes her superposition of studio and home; the Fondazione Merz focuses on her material experiments; and the Castello di Rivoli explores her metaphysical engagement with space. All the while, Merz’s elusive central themes—transparency, metamorphosis, and alchemy—recur throughout.

True to the retrospective’s title, the suite of exhibitions doesn’t follow a chronological itinerary, if only because to do so is nearly impossible. Her biography remains shrouded in mystery. These are the known facts of her life before 1960: Born in Turin to a father employed by Fiat, she studied dance and later modeled in other artists’ studios. Even after garnering critical attention, she rarely titled or dated her compositions and struggled to lay them to rest. The title of her first and best-known installation, The Living Sculpture (1966), says it all, encoding her belief that completion is concomitant to a kind of death.

This unsettled attitude manifests in a provisional quality that prevails across the works on view. The Living Sculpture is a tentacular, sewn-aluminum work that originally dangled claustrophobically from the ceilings of her home and now hangs in glittering fragments at GAM and Castello di Rivoli. Her series of knobby clay “Testine (Little Heads),” made from the 1970s to the 2010s, are unfired and sometimes retain the rough corners with which they were cut in bricklike masses from a larger block of clay. Her abstracted faces, painted and drawn on paper, wood, and alabaster, are warped and blurred as if in motion; one untitled and undated graphite physiognomy rearranges itself in whirling lines of vortex-like eyes.

Merz, like her Arte Povera peers, was frustrated by fixity and drawn to materials that morph across time. Perhaps appropriately, the curators have displayed works that may be unfinished and come straight from the studio; whether she planned to continue them will never be known. Notes on hotel stationery and Post-its remain tacked, taped, and clipped directly onto her drawings and paintings, variably describing the emotions she hoped to capture (for example, “expressive and polished”), quoting from literature (one composition glosses Hölderlin’s final poem), or simply logging dimensions. There is a sense that Merz might yet return with needle, pencil, or brush and pick up where she left off.

As if to show how an idea remains unfixed, persisting and evolving as later generations take it on, the exhibitions stage encounters between Merz and contemporary women artists—including Leonor Antunes, Thea Djordjadze, and Miriam Cahn—whose work shares affinities with hers. Tacita Dean was commissioned to produce a body of film and photographs in Merz’s home and studio. The results include a 16 mm film diptych Via Milano 13 (2026) capturing scenes from Merz’s apartment near Turin’s Porta Palazzo market. In slow frames, we see a honeycombed assemblage of cardboard cylinders from rolls of toilet paper and paper towels; a chorus of “Testine” arranged on the spiraling table in her husband’s old studio; a painted, blue-haired visage with livid red lips fastened on a wall, its double mirrored upside-down in a glass surface below. Hung in constellated installations at GAM and Fondazione Merz, a complementary series of photographs likewise opens Merz’s private world to our curious eyes, often capturing works in situ among furniture and family photographs before their displacement to the exhibitions’ airy galleries. The film and images verge on invasion, contravening Merz’s injunction against photographic capture—except, of course, for the fact of the artist’s absence, palpable in Dean’s meditative, static shots.

Leaving this suite of exhibitions, I find Merz’s practice is even more fugitive than before. I am not the first critic to encounter this difficulty. Writing on her work for Artforum in 1992, Celant reflected, “The instant it is defined, it flees.” Like the artist herself, Merz’s works are chimerical, morphing with the shifting light, blurring at the edges of the frame, slipping out of sight.
excerpt_original: Three venues in Turin honor Arte Povera’s only woman.

title_original: OTHERNETWORK: REDEFINIR LA CULTURA DESDE LAS PERIFERIAS
editorial_excerpt_zh: OtherNetwork 是一个将不同地理位置的独立艺术空间连接起来的国际网络，旨在倍增文化生产与流动的节点。我们与其创始人费德里科·马泰利（Federico Martelli）对话，探讨如何将文化电路去中心化，并从小规模建设长期基础设施和纽带……

{"type": "paragraph", "text": "独立艺术空间通常在物资匮乏的状态下运作：团队规模小、预算不确定，往往结合了自主管理与定向支持。然而，这种不稳定性并不必然意味着缺乏自由。对于 OtherNetwork 的创始人费德里科·马泰利而言，艺术家在这些空间中找到了更大的工作自主权，尤其是在民主制度脆弱或威权政府的背景下。他在那里看到了筹备展览和与艺术家合作的其他方式，受大型机构规则的约束更少。", "links": [{"text": "OtherNetwork", "url": "https://othernetwork.io/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "大流行使这些空间的脆弱性变得更加明显。随之而来的预算削减最终将其彻底摆上台面。它们会怎么样？它们如何能互相帮助？OtherNetwork 的构想正是从这些问题开始成型的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该项目最初由总部位于鹿特丹的设计工作室 Cookies（费德里科·马泰利是该工作室成员）与德国对外文化关系学院（ifa）合作构思。项目始于2021年，旨在连接世界各地的独立空间，并汇集允许它们相互合作的资金。如今，OtherNetwork 作为一个在荷兰注册的非营利基金会运营，其团队分布在欧洲、非洲和拉丁美洲。它的工作一直建立在这些纽带之上，就像一个从组成它的空间和个人出发的网络。", "links": [{"text": "ifa", "url": "https://www.ifa.de/en/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OtherNetwork-event-Voy-y-Vuelvo-2025-Copiapo.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "OtherNetwork 活动。远距艺术研究所，Voy y Vuelvo，2025年，智利科皮亚波。摄影：保利纳·梅拉多（Paulina Mellado）。", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "边缘不是一个地点，而是一种立场", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“边缘”是马泰利有意使用的一个词，因为艺术界的很大一部分人已经学会这样看待独立空间：将其视为存在于一个已经确立的中心之外、周围或对立面的东西。博物馆、商业画廊、大型机构。其他空间则作为卫星在周围轨道运行。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "OtherNetwork 一直在思考，如果颠倒这种等级制度会发生什么，如果这些空间不是去向中心靠拢，而是各自将自己视为一个中心。“如今，定义、讨论和书写文化的方式总是来自中心，这里的中心我指的不仅仅是博物馆，尽管它们是很重要的一部分。我还指的是那些把自己定位为品味风向标的杂志，以及那些撰写评论并决定什么是好什么是坏的地方。那些就是震中，”马泰利断言道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在一个数字互联的世界里，一个艺术现场由许多同时存在的现场构成。中心与边缘的对立可以让位于一种结构，其中多个中心共存，并根据它们之间织造的纽带进行自我定义。因此，边缘质疑了中心作为合法性唯一标准的地位。“一切都变成了网络，一切都变成了节点，每个人都可以为自己宣称中心的一小部分。这就是我们如何玩转边缘概念的方式；归根结底，这是一个提议，”马泰利说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OtherNetwork-event-Digital-Dreams-Analog-Hearts-2024-Kumasi.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "OtherNetwork 活动。阿夸西·贝迪亚科·阿夫拉内（Akwasi Bediako Afrane），《数字梦想：模拟心脏》（Digital Dreams: Analog Hearts），2024年，加纳库马西。摄影：安瓦尔·萨达特·穆罕默德（Anwar Sadat Mohammed）。鸣谢：OtherNetwork", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "什么是独立？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "回答什么是独立空间比听起来要复杂。一些人所理解的自主权，对另一些人来说可能意味着完全不同的事情。马泰利在试图整理组成 OtherNetwork 的空间时遇到了这种困难。“在金沙萨，独立与政治的关系要大得多：免受审查的自由。这是一种深刻的独立形式，在鹿特丹这样的小地方，我们或许认为这是理所当然的。尽管连这也正在改变：随着加沙和以色列局势的发展，文化界承受着保持对种族灭绝沉默的真实压力。这并不总是直接的审查，但能感受得到。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "相比之下，在荷兰，有些空间被认为是独立的，其相当一部分资金来自国家。政治条件和资助模式因语境而异，“独立”一词的含义也随之改变。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该平台本身也不得不面对这种模糊的概念。当与一个国际网络合作时，必须找到能够整理信息和管理的分类，但这些分类往往不足以描述实际发生的事情。因此，OtherNetwork 的首批社论系列之一《相互依存》（Interdependence）邀请了各个空间推荐作者来谈论他们对独立的各自看法。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这一练习并没有完全解决讨论，反而引发了另一个问题：相对于什么的独立？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对于 OtherNetwork 而言，独立是相对于一个空间试图保持自主的事物而言的：国家、市场、某个机构或某个现场的权力结构。但这种自主权可以与其他依赖模式共存。恰恰是这种缺乏单一确定的定义，才使得对话得以继续敞开。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Screenshot-2025-10-31-at-14.49.26.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "OtherNetwork", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一张产生连接的地图", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "OtherNetwork 网站上的地图将各个空间标注在其开展工作的城市和小镇上，而不按国家进行归类。“我们认为，人类生活的尺度是在城市层面，是人与人之间的交往，也正是在这一尺度上，这些独立空间才最具活力和成效。”在马尔特利看来，每个地点身处何方以及它与谁产生联系同样重要。“这张地图不仅记录联系，它还产生并巩固联系。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "实现这一目标的途径之一是接力赛（relay），这是一种由一个东道主空间邀请下一个空间举办展览的接力体制。通过这种方式，一条链条可以从斯图加特开始，延续至阿克拉和约翰内斯堡，随后途经巴西和波多黎各，抵达巴兰基亚，并一直延伸到危地马拉。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该接力项目获得了德国对外文化关系学院（ifa）的资金支持，并由 OtherNetwork 提供伴随支持。OtherNetwork 在制作、传播和其他实际方面提供协助，但不干预各空间的策展决策，因此，新的纽带是从参与者之间形成的联系中自然滋生的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我们变成了一种幽灵般的机构，一个去中心化的博物馆：资金、平面物料、专业支持、传播——博物馆所做的一切我们都做，但却没有博物馆的实体。每一次连接都会催生下一次连接，最重要的是，它建立起了信任，”马尔特利解释道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OtherNetwork-event-Community-Generosity-Longevity-2023-Accra.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "OtherNetwork 活动：Community, Generosity, Longevity ，2023年，加纳阿克拉", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "同样脆弱的网络", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "然而，这一体系的发展中也存在着一个悖论。OtherNetwork 自身的永续性同它试图连接的许多空间一样脆弱。“我们的运作方式有点像一个伞形组织：我们努力展现出专业性，拥有一个了不起的团队，并且投入了我们的大量时间来促成这一切。我们投射出一种稳固扎实的外表，但其实我们和所有人一样脆弱，”马尔特利说道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这一现实促使 OtherNetwork 重新审视其在网络中的地位。如果它自身也是一个独立艺术项目，那它同样无法免于其成员所面临的困境。实际上，它分担了许多同样的问题，就像是一个织锦网络中的普通参与者，所有人都在不同程度上承受着脆弱性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“如果我们自身也是一个独立艺术项目，那我们就是网络内部的同伴，而不是一个提供援助的外部主体，”他解释道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这就迫使该组织思考，在一个成员之间差异可能巨大的环境中该如何分配资源。一些组织拥有巩固的团队和架构，而另一些组织则可能在极限运转。OtherNetwork 试图将这些差异纳入考量，将更多资源投入到最需要它们的地方。其目的是避免一个国际网络去复制它所试图质疑的那些等级秩序。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/espacio-odeon.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "作为其2023年国际文化项目的一部分，OtherNetwork 在哥伦比亚首都的 Odeón 空间举办了首场本土活动，6位受邀嘉宾围绕其在哥伦比亚首都创建、指导或管理独立文化项目的经验展开了讨论。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但这并非总是一帆风顺。各个空间的能力和工作方式各有不同，在合作过程中难免会产生摩擦。对 OtherNetwork 而言，这些摩擦是与互不相识、处境各异的人和组织共事时不可或缺的学习过程。正因如此，便诞生了“应对摩擦”（Navigating Frictions）系列社论，探讨如何在这些差异之间穿梭，并将其融入到网络的构建中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我们试图向摩擦学习。摩擦正是让我们保持活力的源泉，也是大多数这类组织不得不学会应对的东西。我们的角色是驾驭这些动态：充当催化剂，或是各方之间的一种润滑剂，以确保事情真正发生，”马尔特利指出。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这项工作还需要关注可能在网络内部自我复制的权力动态。马尔特利解释说，团队的大部分内部讨论都围绕着如何避免充当“看门人”（gatekeepers），以及如何防止他们正在织就的网络变成又一个文化榨取主义（extractivism）的案例。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从这个意义上说，接力项目也发挥着一定作用，因为它在参与者之间分摊了决策权。他说，其意图是让互联的各方共享能动性，让每个参与者都感到受重视，并使网络的资源和收益得到公正的分配。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OtherNetwork-Event-Eisegetical-Reading-Machine-2025-Aguas-Buenas.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "OtherNetwork 活动。Anamarie，《伊塞格基读书机》（Eisegetical Reading Machine），2025年，波多黎各阿瓜斯布埃纳斯。", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "维持一个网络", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "当然，这一切架构都需要资源。德国对外文化关系学院（ifa）是隶属于外交部的德国机构，从一开始就是 OtherNetwork 的主要合作伙伴。它提供了初始资金，如今则全资资助展览接力项目——这是该网络成本最高、由双方共同开展的活动。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对 ifa 而言，该项目在某种程度上是一场实验。其视觉艺术部四十多年来一直在开发巡回展览，传统上，这些展览是将一个地方创作的作品运往其他目的地，当地的参与度很低。通过与 OtherNetwork 合作，该机构开始尝试一种不同的、延续至今的模式：让独立空间展开对话，并让项目从各自的语境中孕育而生。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "随着时间推移，OtherNetwork 在荷兰注册成立了基金会。出于行政原因，这种法律形式使其能够获得其他资金来源，同时不改变与 ifa 的合作关系——ifa 依然是其主要合作伙伴。该组织还获得了 Stimuleringsfonds 以及知名摄影师沃尔夫冈·蒂尔曼斯（Wolfgang Tillmans）创立的基金会 Between Bridges 等机构的支持。资金来源的多样化仍然是一个挑战，这也是关于“何为独立”这一讨论的一部分。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“除了作为一个申请文化基金的文化项目之外，我们希望能够接触到更具社会导向、致力于强化社会的慈善事业。这并不容易：这些圈子很难进入，我们目前正积极寻找一些线索。此外，我们也开始接受个人捐赠，”马泰利详细说道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OtherNetwork-Exhibition-Los-Limites-del-Afuera-2025-San-Juan-ph-Thais-Llorca-Lezcano.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "“外在的界限”（Los límites del "text": "OtherNetwork 在过程中发现的一点是，数字世界与现实面对面之间的关系最终不同于他们的设想。起初，马泰利认为网页将是项目的核心，而实体聚会只是一种延伸。结果却恰好相反。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“最重要的是活动，是在现实生活中发生的事情，正是这些真实的事情构建了数字平台，”他说道。不过该网站也在同步壮大。它是一个不断增长的档案库。“它起初非常简陋，但如今你可以追溯三年前或更早发生的事情。我们希望它对创作者、策展人以及任何研究文化究竟如何发生的人都有所帮助。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "OtherNetwork 现在明白，其真正的职能是为各个空间建立联系创造条件，更重要的是，让这些纽带在时间中延续。“水口”（Bocas de agua）作为接力展的第六场展览，就是一个很好的例子。这一次，巴兰基亚的梅拉之家（Casa de Meira）邀请了危地马拉安提瓜的新工厂（La Nueva Fábrica）在该市开展创作。该展览于 10 月 15 日至 11 月 12 日在大西洋大学美术馆（Galería de Bellas Artes de la Universidad del Atlántico）展出，汇集了来自哥伦比亚、危地马拉、波多黎各、哥斯达黎加、巴西、特立尼达和多巴哥以及智利的艺术家。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "新工厂总监兼策展人伊拉里亚·孔蒂（Ilaria "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ifa_foundation-for-conceptionary-art_Ghana_067.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "“如果我们能在梦中感到快乐，这还算数吗？”（If we’re happy in our dreams, does that count?）展览现场。ifa 斯图加特画廊，2023 年。由加纳当代艺术基金会策展，作为 OtherNetwork 项目的一部分。摄影：安德烈亚斯·克尔纳（Andreas Körner）", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从小规模做起", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在世界各地面临政治、社会和生态危机的背景下，马泰利重新强调了艺术和文化作为对话空间的重要性。但在 OtherNetwork 的情况下，他并不打算通过建立一个不断扩大的、试图涵盖更多前沿的组织来应对这些局势。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我们的梦想是成为一个更加开放、多元和包容的工具。这些年来，通过这些活动和展览，我们建立了一个类似家庭的社群。我们非常乐意通过更多小规模的机会来维持这些关系，而不是搞宏大项目。小规模正是我们想要耕耘的地方。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这样一个平台的影响力是以年为单位来衡量的。资金来了又去，展览和活动都有闭幕日期，但通过接力相识的两个艺术空间之间的信任却可以长存。OtherNetwork 所提出的乃是一个赌注：只要有耐心，小小的倡议也能留下痕迹。", "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "OtherNetwork es una red internacional que enlaza espacios artísticos independientes de geografías diversas para multiplicar los nodos desde los que la cultura puede producirse y movilizarse. Hablamos con su fundador, Federico Martelli, sobre cómo descentralizar los circuitos culturales y construir infraestructura y vínculos de largo plazo desde la pequeña escala."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Los espacios de arte independientes suelen funcionar con poco: equipos pequeños, presupuestos inciertos, muchas veces una mezcla de autogestión y apoyos puntuales. Pero esa precariedad no necesariamente se traduce en falta de libertad. Para Federico Martelli , fundador de OtherNetwork , los artistas encuentran en estos espacios más autonomía para trabajar, sobre todo en contextos de democracias frágiles o gobiernos autoritarios. Allí percibe otros modos de montar exposiciones y de trabajar con los artistas, menos sujetos a las reglas de las grandes instituciones.", "links": [{"text": "OtherNetwork", "url": "https://othernetwork.io/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "La pandemia hizo más evidente la fragilidad de esos espacios. Los recortes presupuestarios que vinieron después terminaron de ponerla sobre la mesa. ¿Qué pasaría con ellos? ¿Cómo podían ayudarse entre sí? La idea de OtherNetwork comenzó a tomar forma a partir de esas preguntas."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "El proyecto fue concebido originalmente por el estudio de diseño Cookies , con sede en Rotterdam, del que forma parte Federico Martelli, en colaboración con el Institut für Auslandsbeziehungen ( ifa ) de Alemania. Iniciado en 2021, buscaba conectar espacios independientes de diferentes partes del mundo y reunir los fondos que les permitieran colaborar entre sí. Hoy, OtherNetwork opera como una fundación sin fines de lucro registrada en los Países Bajos, con un equipo distribuido entre Europa, África y América Latina. Su trabajo se ha ido armando desde esos vínculos, como una red que parte de los espacios y las personas que la componen.", "links": [{"text": "ifa", "url": "https://www.ifa.de/en/"}]}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/OtherNetwork-event-Voy-y-Vuelvo-2025-Copiapo.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Evento de OtherNetwork. Instituto Tele Arte, Voy y Vuelvo , 2025, Copiapó, Chile. Foto: Paulina Mellado.", "credit": "Artishock"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Periferia no como lugar, sino como posición"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Periferia” es una palabra que Martelli usa a propósito, porque así es como buena parte del mundo del arte ha aprendido a mirar a los espacios independientes: como aquello que está fuera, alrededor o frente a un centro que ya estaría establecido. article_text:
OtherNetwork es una red internacional que enlaza espacios artísticos independientes de geografías diversas para multiplicar los nodos desde los que la cultura puede producirse y movilizarse. Hablamos con su fundador, Federico Martelli, sobre cómo descentralizar los circuitos culturales y construir infraestructura y vínculos de largo plazo desde la pequeña escala.

Los espacios de arte independientes suelen funcionar con poco: equipos pequeños, presupuestos inciertos, muchas veces una mezcla de autogestión y apoyos puntuales. Pero esa precariedad no necesariamente se traduce en falta de libertad. Para Federico Martelli , fundador de OtherNetwork , los artistas encuentran en estos espacios más autonomía para trabajar, sobre todo en contextos de democracias frágiles o gobiernos autoritarios. Allí percibe otros modos de montar exposiciones y de trabajar con los artistas, menos sujetos a las reglas de las grandes instituciones.

La pandemia hizo más evidente la fragilidad de esos espacios. Los recortes presupuestarios que vinieron después terminaron de ponerla sobre la mesa. ¿Qué pasaría con ellos? ¿Cómo podían ayudarse entre sí? La idea de OtherNetwork comenzó a tomar forma a partir de esas preguntas.

El proyecto fue concebido originalmente por el estudio de diseño Cookies , con sede en Rotterdam, del que forma parte Federico Martelli, en colaboración con el Institut für Auslandsbeziehungen ( ifa ) de Alemania. Iniciado en 2021, buscaba conectar espacios independientes de diferentes partes del mundo y reunir los fondos que les permitieran colaborar entre sí. Hoy, OtherNetwork opera como una fundación sin fines de lucro registrada en los Países Bajos, con un equipo distribuido entre Europa, África y América Latina. Su trabajo se ha ido armando desde esos vínculos, como una red que parte de los espacios y las personas que la componen.

Periferia no como lugar, sino como posición

“Periferia” es una palabra que Martelli usa a propósito, porque así es como buena parte del mundo del arte ha aprendido a mirar a los espacios independientes: como aquello que está fuera, alrededor o frente a un centro que ya estaría establecido. Museos, galerías comerciales, grandes instituciones. Los demás orbitan como satélites.

OtherNetwork se ha preguntado siempre qué ocurre si se invierte esa jerarquía, si, en lugar de acercar esos espacios al centro, cada uno pudiera pensarse como un centro en sí mismo. “Hoy, la manera en que la cultura se define, se discute y se escribe siempre viene del centro, y por centro no me refiero solo a los museos, aunque son una parte importante. También me refiero a las revistas que se posicionan como referentes del gusto, a los lugares donde se escribe crítica y se decide qué es bueno y qué no. Esos son los epicentros”, afirma Martelli.

En un mundo digitalmente interconectado, una escena artística está hecha de muchas escenas simultáneas. La oposición entre centro y periferia puede dar paso a una estructura donde coexisten múltiples centros que se definen según los vínculos que se tejen entre ellos. La periferia, entonces, cuestiona la existencia del centro como única medida de legitimidad. “Todo se vuelve red, todo se vuelve nodo, y cada uno puede reclamar un pedacito del centro para sí. Así es como jugamos con la noción de periferia; en el fondo, es una propuesta”, dice Martelli.

¿Qué significa ser independiente?

Responder qué es un espacio independiente es más complejo de lo que parece. Lo que algunos entienden como autonomía, para otros puede significar algo completamente distinto. Martelli se encontró con esa dificultad al intentar ordenar los espacios que integran OtherNetwork. “En Kinshasa, la independencia tiene mucho más que ver con lo político: la libertad de no ser censurado. Es una forma profunda de independencia, una que quizás damos por sentada en un lugar como Rotterdam. Aunque incluso eso está cambiando: con la situación en Gaza e Israel, hay una presión real en la escena cultural para guardar silencio sobre el genocidio. No siempre es censura directa, pero se siente”.

En los Países Bajos, en cambio, hay espacios que se consideran independientes y que reciben una proporción considerable de su financiamiento del Estado. Las condiciones políticas y los modelos de financiamiento varían de un contexto a otro, y con ellos cambia también el significado de la palabra “independiente”.

La propia plataforma tuvo que enfrentarse a esa noción difusa. Cuando se trabaja con una red internacional, hay que encontrar categorías que permitan ordenar la información y la gestión, pero esas categorías no siempre alcanzan para describir lo que ocurre en la práctica. Por eso, una de las primeras series editoriales de OtherNetwork, Interdependence , invitó a diversos espacios a proponer autores que hablaran de sus propias ideas sobre la independencia.

El ejercicio no resolvió del todo la discusión y despertó otra pregunta: ¿independiente respecto de qué?

Para OtherNetwork, la independencia se entiende frente a aquello de lo que un espacio busca mantenerse autónomo: el Estado, el mercado, una institución o las estructuras de poder de una escena. Pero esa autonomía puede convivir con otros modos de dependencia. Justamente, esa falta de una definición única es la que permite que la conversación siga abierta.

Un mapa que produce conexiones

El mapa del sitio web de OtherNetwork ubica a los espacios en las ciudades y pueblos donde desarrollan su trabajo, sin agruparlos por países. “Creemos que es a escala de ciudad donde vivimos como humanos, de persona a persona, y ahí es donde estos espacios independientes son más activos y efectivos”. Para Martelli, importa dónde está cada lugar y también con quién se vincula. “El mapa no solo registra conexiones, también las produce y las fortalece”.

Una de las vías para lograrlo es el relay , un sistema de relevo en el que un espacio anfitrión invita al siguiente a realizar una exposición. Así, una cadena puede comenzar en Stuttgart, continuar en Accra y Johannesburgo, pasar luego por Brasil y Puerto Rico, llegar a Barranquilla y seguir hasta Guatemala.

El relay cuenta con el financiamiento de ifa y con el acompañamiento de OtherNetwork, que aporta apoyo en producción, comunicación y otros aspectos prácticos, pero no interviene en las decisiones curatoriales de los espacios, de modo que los nuevos vínculos surgen de los lazos que se forman entre quienes participan.

“Nos convertimos en una especie de institución fantasma, un museo descentralizado: financiamiento, material gráfico, apoyo profesional, comunicación; todo lo que hace un museo, pero sin el museo. Cada conexión genera la siguiente y, sobre todo, construye confianza”, explica Martelli.

Una red también precaria

Hay, sin embargo, una paradoja en el desarrollo de este sistema. La sostenibilidad de OtherNetwork es tan frágil como la de muchos de los espacios que busca enlazar. “Funcionamos un poco como una organización paraguas: intentamos ser profesionales, tenemos un equipo maravilloso, le dedicamos mucho de nuestro propio tiempo a que esto ocurra. Proyectamos la sensación de ser algo asentado y sólido, pero somos tan precarios como todos los demás”, afirma Martelli.

Esta constatación ha llevado a OtherNetwork a replantear su lugar dentro de la red. Si es también un proyecto independiente, tampoco queda a salvo de las dificultades que enfrentan sus miembros. En realidad, comparte muchos de sus problemas, como un participante más de una trama en la que todos tienen distintos grados de vulnerabilidad.

“Si nosotros también somos un proyecto de arte independiente, entonces somos pares dentro de la red, no un agente externo que ofrece ayuda”, explica.

Esto obliga a la organización a pensar cómo se distribuyen los recursos en un entorno donde las diferencias entre los miembros pueden ser enormes. Mientras algunas organizaciones cuentan con equipos y estructuras consolidadas, otras pueden estar funcionando al límite de su capacidad. OtherNetwork intenta tener esas diferencias en cuenta y poner más recursos donde hacen más falta. El objetivo es evitar que una red internacional reproduzca las mismas jerarquías que pretende cuestionar.

El primer evento local organizado por OtherNetwork como parte de su programa cultural internacional de 2023 se llevó a cabo en Espacio Odeón, en el que seis invitados hablaron sobre su experiencia en la creación, dirección o gestión de proyectos culturales independientes en la capital colombiana.

Pero no siempre es fácil. Las capacidades y modos de trabajo de cada espacio difieren, y al colaborar pueden surgir fricciones. Para OtherNetwork, esas fricciones son un aprendizaje inherente al trabajar entre personas y organizaciones que no se conocen, en contextos diferentes. De ahí surge Navigating Frictions , una serie de editoriales sobre cómo moverse entre esas diferencias e incorporarlas a la construcción de la red.

“Intentamos aprender de la fricción. La fricción es lo que nos mantiene vivos, es con lo que la mayoría de estas organizaciones ha tenido que aprender a lidiar. Nuestro rol es navegar esas dinámicas: ser un catalizador, o una especie de lubricante entre las partes, para asegurarnos de que las cosas realmente pasen”, señala Martelli.

Ese trabajo también exige atender a las dinámicas de poder que pueden reproducirse dentro de la propia red. Martelli explica que gran parte de las conversaciones internas del equipo gira en torno a cómo evitar actuar como gatekeepers y cómo impedir que lo que están tejiendo se convierta en un caso más de extractivismo cultural.

El relay también cumple una función en ese sentido, porque reparte la toma de decisiones entre quienes participan. La intención, dice, es que las partes vinculadas compartan agencia, que cada participante se sienta valorado y que los recursos y beneficios de la red se distribuyan de forma justa.

Sostener una red

Toda esta estructura necesita, por supuesto, recursos. ifa, institución alemana vinculada al Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores, es desde el inicio el principal socio de OtherNetwork. Aportó el financiamiento inicial y hoy financia íntegramente el relay de exposiciones, la actividad más costosa de la red, que ambas organizaciones desarrollan en conjunto.

Para ifa, el proyecto fue en parte un experimento. Su Departamento de Artes Visuales lleva más de cuarenta años desarrollando exposiciones itinerantes, que tradicionalmente trasladaban obras producidas en un lugar hacia otros destinos, con poca participación local. Junto a OtherNetwork, la institución se abrió a probar un modelo distinto, que sigue vigente: poner en conversación a espacios independientes y dejar que los proyectos se hagan desde sus propios contextos.

Con el tiempo, OtherNetwork se constituyó como fundación en los Países Bajos. Por razones administrativas, esa figura le permite acceder a otras fuentes de financiamiento, sin cambiar el vínculo con ifa, que sigue siendo su socio principal. La organización también ha recibido apoyo de instituciones como Stimuleringsfonds y Between Bridges , la fundación que creó el reconocido fotógrafo Wolfgang Tillmans. Diversificar las fuentes de financiamiento sigue siendo un desafío, y es parte de la conversación sobre qué significa ser independiente.

“Más allá de ser un proyecto cultural que postula a fondos culturales, esperamos acceder a una filantropía con un enfoque más social, orientada a fortalecer la sociedad. No ha sido fácil: son círculos difíciles de entrar y estamos siguiendo activamente algunas pistas. Además, nos estamos abriendo a donaciones individuales”, detalla Martelli.

Del mapa digital al encuentro físico

Una de las cosas que OtherNetwork descubrió en el camino fue que la relación entre lo digital y lo presencial terminó siendo distinta de lo que habían imaginado. Al comienzo, Martelli pensaba que la página web sería el centro del proyecto y que los encuentros físicos funcionarían como una extensión. Ocurrió exactamente al revés.

“Lo más importante terminaron siendo los eventos, las cosas que se hacen en la vida real, y son esas cosas reales las que construyen la plataforma digital”, cuenta. Pero el sitio web se fortalece en paralelo. Es un archivo en constante crecimiento. “Partió muy esquelético, pero hoy puedes rastrear cosas que pasaron hace tres años o más. Esperamos que sea útil para creadores, curadores y para cualquiera que estudie cómo ocurre realmente la cultura”.

OtherNetwork entiende ahora que su verdadera función es generar las condiciones para que los espacios se vinculen y, más importante aún, para que esos nexos continúen en el tiempo. Bocas de agua , la sexta exposición del relay, es un buen ejemplo. Esta vez, Casa de Meira , en Barranquilla, invitó a La Nueva Fábrica , de Antigua Guatemala, a desarrollar una propuesta en la ciudad. La exposición se presenta del 15 de octubre al 12 de noviembre en la Galería de Bellas Artes de la Universidad del Atlántico y reúne a artistas de Colombia, Guatemala, Puerto Rico, Costa Rica, Brasil, Trinidad y Tobago y Chile.

Ilaria Conti , directora y curadora de La Nueva Fábrica, toma como punto de partida Barranquilla y su diálogo con el río Magdalena y el Caribe para organizar esta exposición en torno al agua, la interdependencia y los vínculos entre cuerpos, territorios y saberes.

Trabajar desde la pequeña escala

En medio de crisis políticas, sociales y ecológicas en distintas partes del mundo, Martelli reivindica la importancia del arte y la cultura como espacios de diálogo. Pero, en el caso de OtherNetwork, no imagina responder a estas circunstancias con una organización cada vez más grande que busque cubrir más frentes.

“El sueño es convertirnos en una herramienta más abierta, diversa y accesible. En estos años hemos construido una especie de familia a través de estos eventos y exposiciones. Nos encantaría mantener vivas esas relaciones con más oportunidades a pequeña escala, no megaproyectos. La pequeña escala es donde queremos trabajar”.

El impacto de una plataforma como esta se mide en años. Los fondos llegan y se acaban, las exposiciones y eventos tienen fecha de cierre, pero la confianza entre dos espacios de arte que se conocieron a través de un relevo puede perdurar. Lo que propone OtherNetwork es una apuesta: que las iniciativas pequeñas, con paciencia, dejen huella.
excerpt_original: OtherNetwork es una red internacional que enlaza espacios artísticos independientes de geografías diversas para multiplicar los nodos desde los que la cultura puede producirse y movilizarse. Hablamos con su fundador, Federico Martelli, sobre cómo descentralizar los circuitos…

article_text:
Oscar-nominated composer Daniel Pemberton is a quadruple threat — at least — this year with scores in four movies, as well as the TV series “Slow Horses.”

The British film music writer composed the soundtracks to movies including “The Drama,” with its mischievous flutes recorded at Abbey Road Studios; “Masters of the Universe”; and Oscar contenders “Ink,” “ Project Hail Mary ,” and “Musk.” On this week’s edition of IndieWire’s “ Screen Talk ” podcast, co-hosts Anne Thompson and Ryan Lattanzio spoke to Pemberton about his multi-hyphenate journey to composing, which began in video games but included breakout work on Ridley Scott’s “The Counselor.”

“With ‘Hail Mary,’ it was like it had no map, and it was like we gotta make this up as we go along. And that’s thrilling, but also terrifying. And so we spent a huge amount of time, like, just trying out ideas, experimenting, finding unusual textures and sounds, approaches, and that would slowly feed itself into the movie or end up in the bin,” said Pemberton, who also wrote an original song called “Let Me Sell You a Dream” that’s sung by David Byrne in Alex Gibney’s “Musk.” ( Gibney was the special guest on last week’s episode of “Screen Talk.” )

Elsewhere on the podcast, we also review (i.e., eviscerate) Taika Waititi’s confoundingly awful dystopian sci-fi movie “ Klara and the Sun ,” an adaptation of Nobel Prize-winning author Kazuo Ishiguro and starring Jenna Ortega, who’s on a big-screen losing streak after terrible reviews for her last several movies. Like her co-star Amy Adams, she’s faring better these days on television (see Netflix’s “Wednesday”).

We also catch up on “I Play Rocky” and the latest developments in the awards season race — plus, the C-suite freefall happening at Netflix amid the ousting of film head Dan Lin.

Listen to the episode below or on your preferred podcast platform.

article_text:
“ You Can See Everything ,” an intimate look at Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, has earned nearly $80 million at the domestic box office , becoming A24 ‘s third-highest-grossing release in North America. It bypasses “Everything Everywhere All at Once” and its $77 million haul to take its spot on the indie studio’s chart, and that film won the Oscar for Best Picture.

With $79.8 million stateside, “You Can See Everything” sits behind the summer blockbuster “Backrooms” ($197 million) and 2025’s “Marty Supreme” ($96 million) on the list of A24 releases. Other A24 films made more globally, with “Backrooms” earning more than $400 million, “Marty Supreme” grossing $192.4 million, and “Everything Everywhere All at Once” netting $147.9 million.

However, “You Can See Everything” has yet to be released in most international markets. It’s unclear if Holmes’ fraud will resonate with moviegoers so far from Silicon Valley. It doesn’t matter if it doesn’t connect, because with a budget of $7 million, “You Can See Everything” is already wildly profitable. Its success means that Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, the directing duo behind the doc, are now in high demand.

“You Can See Everything” also jumped ahead of “March of the Penguins” ($77 million) on the list of highest-grossing documentaries in North America. Variety reports that makes it the second highest-grossing doc behind Michael Moore’s “Fahrenheit 9/11,” which earned $119 million domestically. That doesn’t account for music documentaries like “Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour” ($267.1 million) and “Michael Jackson’s This is It” ($268 million), which were far more popular.

A24 is on a hot streak . In addition to “Backrooms,” the indie studio has released hits like “The Drama” and “Primetime.” Its latest film, “ Club Kid ,” grossed an impressive $390,583 this weekend when it opened on six screens in New York and Los Angeles. That’s a per-screen average of $65,097. A24 acquired the drama about a hard-living gay man and his son out of the Cannes Film Festival, where it debuted to raves. The studio hopes to position the film and its writer, director, and star Jordan Firstman in the Oscar race.

article_text:
Films and events

First Feature Competition

Lady

In a bustling Lagos, a solitary female taxi driver finds community among a group of sex workers as she transports them around the city.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director-screenwriter Olive Nwosu

With Jessica Gabriel’s Ujah, Amanda Oruh, Tinuade Jemiseye

UK-Nigeria 2026. 93min

Courtesy of Metis Films

Language Nigerian Pidgin With English subtitles

Access information

Saturday 10 October 21:00

Audio description

Tuesday 13 October 12:10

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Lady works long and lonely hours, saving up money with hopes of escaping to Freetown, in Sierra Leone. When childhood friend and sex worker Pinky asks for her help, Lady agrees but soon finds her life upended. The fantastic, mainly female cast shared the Sundance Film Festival Special Jury Award for Acting Ensemble. It’s easy to see why, with this character-driven film that is also a stunning portrait of a vibrant, sleepless city.

Grace Barber-Plentie

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, nudity, and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

Clarissa

Sophie Okonedo shines in Arie and Chuko Esiri’s (Eyimofe, LFF 2020) sophomore feature film, a delicate, sun-soaked re-imagining of Mrs Dalloway, set in contemporary Lagos.

Filipiñana

This bold debut, set over the course of one sweltering day, follows a 17-year-old working as a ‘tee-girl’ at a golf club.

Our Share of Sand

Shalini Adnani’s poignant coming-of-age drama presents a unique perspective on India’s gaping class inequality, child labour and the deep corruption underpinning a family’s economic status.

title_original: Why Good Voice Acting Doesn’t Have to Happen in Isolation
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Film is always a collaborative medium, but one of the special things about animation is that you can craft incredibly nuanced performances with people who never get to meet. Voice acting in animation is a discipline in its own right — as legends like Mel Blanc and Eric Bauza show — where actors impart a kind of electric energy that carries through into the art style of what they’re voicing. So is voice directing. And the secret to both is in providing foundations for animators to build something bigger.", "links": [{"text": "Film", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/film/"}, {"text": "animation", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/news/business/eric-bauza-final-looney-tunes-film-in-theaters-dies-1235226076/"}, {"text": "Voice acting", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/features/animation/legend-of-vox-machina-voice-acting-interview-1235050332/"}, {"text": "animation", "url": "https://www.indiewire.com/t/animation/"}, {"text": "Eric Bauza", "url": "https://www.gofundme.com/f/support-for-ryker-and-jessica-after-eric-bauzas-passing"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“ Wildwood ” director Travis Knight did a lot of the directing of his voice cast in lockdown Zooms, and hodge-podge recording setups, where it can be hard to remember that you’re developing something that needs to spiritually connect to the animation, whether existing animatics already exist or not. article_text:
Film is always a collaborative medium, but one of the special things about animation is that you can craft incredibly nuanced performances with people who never get to meet. Voice acting in animation is a discipline in its own right — as legends like Mel Blanc and Eric Bauza show — where actors impart a kind of electric energy that carries through into the art style of what they’re voicing. So is voice directing. And the secret to both is in providing foundations for animators to build something bigger.

“ Wildwood ” director Travis Knight did a lot of the directing of his voice cast in lockdown Zooms, and hodge-podge recording setups, where it can be hard to remember that you’re developing something that needs to spiritually connect to the animation, whether existing animatics already exist or not. There isn’t the same kind of immersiveness for actors that live-action sets, costumes, and the basic pleasure of getting to read lines against other actors all provide. They have to build it from scratch.

“It asks something very different of an actor, which is challenging because an actor can bring so much to performance before they even utter a word,” Knight told IndieWire on an episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit podcast. “So when you cast these things, it’s really interesting because sometimes the things we love about actors are not their voice; it’s everything else. So we will always listen, we’ll take clips from actors’ other films and their interviews, and we’ll put them against a design of a character.”

Hearing a voice against a design can be revelatory, Knight believes, because it can teach a director and an animation team about who a character really is, whether a performer is really going to work or not, even before they step into the booth. It’s also an important way to help sort the whole of an ensemble so that actors occupy different aural frequencies and accents, and don’t sound too similar. You want to really be able to feel the difference between Carey Mulligan’s powerfully sinister Alexandra and Angela Bassett’s regal General.

And then, once the voice cast is in the booth, it’s also on the director and the team to help each voice actor sketch out all the different permutations of emotion the animators will then use as inspiration, and as tools.

“You’ll get the scene 30, 40, 50 different ways,” Knight said. “It takes forever. But, in the end, if you can do it properly, it feels like these characters are living in the same scene at the same time. And then it comes down to the animator to try to figure out how they can match the beauty of the vocal performance with the physical performance.”

That’s the normal process for feature animation: finding compelling voices, matching them with a design that feels spiritually connected to that voice, covering the performance many different ways, and then assembling a template for animators to build off of. And it’s the director, really, who has to hold in their head the many ways that the disparate parts will all come together.

“An animator is an actor, but they’re just acting through their hands and through a puppet, and it’s two actors collaborating to create a complete performance. But oftentimes it happens across space, across time. And when it comes together in a harmonious way, it’s really beautiful because this thing seems like it’s completely alive,” Knight said.

But sometimes, voice actors’ performances do get to be alive together . That was a key creative choice that director Leah Nelson made for “Tangles” — it’s hard to argue with the logic of putting Abbi Jacobson, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, and Bryan Cranston all in a room together to act out an earnest family drama, even if there’s a bit of mic bleed.

“I’m so glad we [put them together]. And it wasn’t that hard. It took a little bit of scheduling Tetris to get it done, but it was so worthwhile,” Nelson told IndieWire. “Abbi does a ton of voice work, and often they’re alone and not even able to have someone to read against them. Sometimes they’re just doing the lines and sort of jumping around. And what I ultimately wanted was to have this really naturalistic dialogue.”

“Tangles” boasts naturalism when it comes to sound, from bespoke foley to overlapping banter that isn’t meant to be precisely understood but to convey the chaos of one’s own (infuriating, loving) family. So Nelson and her team embraced the ways actors can build on each other, and even on improv, in recording the dialogue.

“A lot of humor came out of giving them time to not only play with the dialogue but to play with each other. But also, those really intimate and difficult moments of the film, they could look in each other’s eyes and work through those moments. That was important to me, and it was important to them as well. So it was an experience we all went through together.”

The one downside of treating recording sessions more like the rehearsals for a play is the risk of wrecking takes. “We spent a lot of time at the table trying to hold [our reactions] in or like, ‘Don’t sneeze! Nobody move!’” Nelson joked. “But I didn’t want it to sound like there was so much suturing; the mastery of the dialogue editing to make it all sound naturalistic, so we also did a lot of work to make that happen. But what we had to work with felt very naturalistic to begin with.”

The ultimate example of naturalistic voice acting, however, might be on display in “Wildwood.” Knight’s own son was a newborn while the team was laying down track for the film, which made him the perfect actor for the role of kidnapped Baby Mac.

“I essentially chased him around the house with a digital recorder. Sometimes with my iPhone. I was just trying to coax things out of him, make him laugh and giggle and verbalize. And the thing about babies is that they’re constantly trying to make sense of the world,” Knight said. “They’re always babbling and trying to make shapes with their mouths. So we have a lot of that babbling in the movie, and it helped make it feel naturalistic.”

It speaks to the wide-ranging power of voice acting in animation: you can get to naturalism through a grounded collaboration between actors, an actor in complete isolation, or hitting “record” on an iPhone while you’re changing a diaper.

“Wildwood” is now in theaters. “Tangles” releases in theaters on January 15, 2027.

Editor’s note: T his story contains details of alleged sexual offenses that some readers may find distressing .

Russell Brand was told he “has a platform with followers in the millions” and has not been “taken apart by the media” during questioning by the prosecution today at Southwark Crown Court.

Brand was being probed by barrister Riel Karmy-Jones over his attacks on the press after allegations were made in a Channel 4 documentary and in The Times in 2023, which led six women to go to the police with similar allegations about him.

Related Stories

Russell Brand Forcefully Denies Charges As He Gives Evidence During Rape Trial: "Consent Is More Important Than Sex Itself"

CNN's Scott Jennings Hit With $72.5M Suit By Hasan Piker Over "Manipulated" Lynching Misquote

Brand has repeatedly criticized large portions of the media for the way in which he has been portrayed since 2023 and uses his Rumble social media platform to communicate his message.

Watch on Deadline

While Brand earlier told the court “no one will touch me with a bargepole” since the documentary, Karmy-Jones said it is “not the case you have been completely abandoned by everyone,” as she pointed out he was playing a show to a packed house of around 2,000 people in London when the doc came out.

“You have a platform with followers in the millions, don’t you?” she told the court. “This is not a case of ‘Poor Mr Brand’ who’s been taken apart by the media and the social construct.”

At this point in proceedings, the judge told Karmy-Jones to move on with her questioning.

Just before that, when it was put to him that the media had been “very fair” to him by allowing him to respond in detail to the documentary’s allegations before it aired, Brand said he “would reject that quite strongly.”

He vociferously responded “Yes” to the question of whether he “blames” Channel 4’s Dispatches show and the media more broadly for the situation he currently finds himself in.

Brand was told by Karmy-Jones he had been “liberally speaking” about portions of the media and these allegations on his own platform since being charged, but he responded by saying he “has done my very best to respect this judicial process and the integrity of this court.”

Brand was cross-examined by the prosecution after facing questions from his defense lawyer Ian Winter , during which he forcefully denied the charges and said his “entire life has been consumed by these allegations.” Brand faces three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault and now one of attempted indecent assault, reduced from indecent assault, based on allegations made by six women . Deadline has been reporting daily from a live video feed of the courtroom since the trial began.

Pressed on why it is only recently, and after his police interviews, that he has started recalling details of the three rape allegations, Brand said it has “taken a lot of focus and recollection to do the best I can to participate in this.”

Regarding Complainant 1, who alleges Brand raped her in a hotel room at the fringes of the Labour Party conference in 1999, he rejected the idea that he “stood in between her and the exit” and “pushed her on the bed against her will.”

Instead, he recalled he “asked for more than [C1’s] consent.”

Regarding Complainant 3, who alleges Brand orally raped her in a toilet cubicle at a birthday party, Brand denied “pulling her head down violently onto your penis” as it was put to him by Karmy-Jones.

“You liked ejaculating without a condom, and you ejaculated into her mouth,” questioned Karmy-Jones. “You said, ‘Don’t be a spoilsport, come on?’”

Brand replied “no” loudly to these questions. He acknowledged it was “within the bounds of possibility” that a rapist could hold someone’s head down and perform forced oral sex in such a way.

On Complainant 5, who alleges Brand anally raped her at his flat after they’d had consensual vaginal sex, Brand denied the allegation and said he “did not view [C5] as just a hole,” as C5 had claimed.

He said he could not remember C5 leaving blood and feces on his sheets, as she has alleged. He said “recollections increased” of C5 after he watched police interviews of her accusations and remembered she was the “memorable young woman” who had put her tongue in his anus after a play he performed. This was a few days before the alleged anal rape took place.

Goal To Sleep With 5,000 Women

Karmy-Jones repeatedly brought up Brand’s promiscuity during the era the allegations were alleged to have taken place.

He was questioned about a conversation in the car he had with his old flatmate on the way to the Labour conference in 1999, when he was accused of saying he had a goal to sleep with 5,000 women. “While I don’t remember, it’s entirely possible it’s the kind of banter I would have engaged in when I was 24,” he said.

He was accused of “doing anything” to get women into bed with him but retorted that “the way this has been characterized is so nefarious, unpleasant and ugly that it is difficult to answer in earnest.”

Asked if he had said he would not leave a situation with a woman without a conquest, he said: “That sounds specifically like a riff on a Woody Allen joke when he said the only advice my dad ever gave me on his death bed was ‘always try and f*** the waitress’.”

The trial continues.

article_text:
New York Newsletter

A Marquee Week of Indulgence

The latest from the fall auctions, museum protests, and tackling the British Empire one video at a time.

My mom called me greedy in jest this weekend because I had the gall to eat … more than five (but fewer than 10!) square slices of a delicious ube cake in her presence. Unlike each savored bite of that addictive purple pastry, I took her criticism on the chin because I believe that greed and indulgence function as a Venn diagram rather than as synonyms. And because there was still plenty of cake to go around.

Indulgence is in the air right now, and not just because we’re closing in on Thanksgiving weekend. Marquee auctions have rolled in like a thick fog on Monday, not long after the ADAA fair and an adjunctive torrential downpour rinsed the last of art fair season out of New York late last week. A press release from Sotheby’s informed me that $1.1 billion worth of art will go under the hammer this month, underpinned by today’s sale of a rarely seen van Gogh landscape expected to fetch a record-breaking $180 million. A brief shakeup ensued less than a week before the painting goes to auction, as the descendants of its former owner suddenly called on Sotheby’s to withdraw the work , alleging that it was sold under duress due to Nazi persecution.

Don’t worry, though — the auction house shared in a follow-up release that the descendants and the Blaquier-Arrieta family, who are selling the painting alongside 11 other multimillion-dollar masterpieces from their collection, have come to a “mutually satisfactory resolution” that allows the sale to proceed as scheduled.

Really glad they worked that out.

On the other side of the same coin, protesters gathered outside of the Museum of Modern Art during an annual benefit for the museum’s Debra and Leon Black Family Film Center last Thursday, calling on filmmaker and honored guest Steven Spielberg to reject the recognition and boycott the museum over Leon Black’s Epstein-related sexual abuse allegations. Cold, biting rain soaked the group of 20 artists and activists outside the gala, and Spielberg hasn’t acknowledged their demands.

All things considered, Iraqi-British data journalist and illustrator Mona Chalabi’s first-ever book, which was released last week, comes at a most opportune time. The book, Ten Lives: How What We Have Shapes Who We Are (2026), comes from Chalabi five-year endeavor in examining class inequality in the United States by analyzing the incomes, expenses, tax deductions, systemic barriers, and livelihoods of 10 Americans across the nation. In a recent interview with Hyperallergic ’s Lakshmi Rivera Amin, Chalabi noted that journalists themselves often don’t acknowledge or even recognize how their own class upbringing can color their reporting on wealth and poverty, whereas other markers like race and gender are positioned as lenses of understanding.

A new video exhibition on the High Line also tackles greed and indulgence through the lens of the British Empire’s storied trade monopolies and resource theft across South Asia and China. Works by Shahzia Sikander and the artist duo Hylozoic/Desires unpack the British stronghold on salt in India and the empire’s deliberate opium influx in China during the Qing dynasty, while also highlighting historic and speculative subversions that disrupt dominant colonial narratives.

I wasn’t super fond of the High Line’s most recent film installation, but this one sounds more up my alley on a subjective, personal history level. I’m looking forward to checking it out soon — before the weather really turns south — and visiting the Mighty Miniatures exhibition that’s opening this Saturday at the National Museum of the American Indian.

Study Contemporary Art at Sotheby's Institute

Whether you’re pursuing a degree, developing your professional expertise, or deepening your knowledge of contemporary art, discover opportunities to learn from specialists and engage directly with the international art world.

Learn more

From Our Critics

Stephanie Wambugu

Mary Lovelace O’Neal: Requiem at Boesky Gallery

"O’Neal’s compositions transmit a powerful sense of presence and force, as though inviting viewers into the vicarious experience of an artist grappling with the formal concerns of color and line before transcending them."

Amy Levine-Kennedy

American Society of Botanical Artists 29th Annual International Exhibition at the Society of Illustrators

"Here is awe for Mother Earth and her plants — and these botanical artists — and for the meticulous, enchanting detail and outcry that cherish every bud, stem, leaf, petal, bark, seed, blade, stamen, and root."

Phillip Pyle

Octopus and Others: Acts of Collaboration and Poetics at El Museo del Barrio

"The message that passes through could resonate with any of the works that surround it: 'My thoughts have meandered with the footsteps I have walked, heading on this journey to a place I call home.'"

Interviews

Mona Chalabi Paints a Picture of Class Inequality

“The crisis is the system that we’re in,” the Pulitzer Prize-winning data journalist and artist says in an interview with Hyperallergic about her first book, “Ten Lives.” | Lakshmi Rivera Amin

Read More

How Miles Greenberg Got “WAR” Past the Censors

“There was not a single outlet, institution, or gallery that wanted to get behind this thing,” the artist told Hyperallergic about his new, six-hour performance piece. | Phillip Pyle

Read More

What Else Is Happening?

At the Bard Graduate Center, design researcher Yelena McLane takes an audience into the world of Soviet design principles through the lens of influential monthly magazine Decorative Art of the USSR (1957–91) , a critical platform for diversity and innovation in industrial design, interior decor, crafts, folk art, and monumental and decorative architecture across the Soviet Republics. (Wed Nov 18) [ bgc.bard.edu ]

Stewards of local historic and cultural landmarks across Queens share the stories of behind their sites and invite the next generation to engage with the borough’s diverse history in a talk at the Lewis Latimer House in Flushing (Thu Nov 19) [ Instagram flyer ]

Perhaps an institutional complement to HBO's Sex and the City , the Museum of the City of New York opens its Photography Triennial devoted to night time hours in the Big Apple. Midnight snacks, the third shift, and NYC's world-famous nightlife scene are centered in this group exhibition of contemporary photography. (Fri Nov 20) [ mcny.org ]

Part of Amant’s programming for Sentient Earth , exhibiting artists Emil Martirosian and Rachel Fäth will stage a live electronic sound performance complemented by time-based media touching on the show’s themes of extractive industries and their interference with earth’s natural frequencies. (Fri Nov 20) [ amant.org ]

The Whitney celebrates 25 years of artport , its online gallery space for web art commissions, in a phygital exhibition on its sixth floor. (Sat, Nov 21) [ whitney.org ]

The Smithsonian's National Museum of the American Indian opens Mighty Miniatures , a collection exhibition on bite-sized Indigenous art and its monumental role in preserving traditional knowledge, stimulating economic development, and stoking children's imaginations. (Sat Nov 21) [ americanindian.si.edu ]

editorial_title_zh: 巴利亚多利德电影节吸引全球大师、30场世界首映及西班牙新锐人才
editorial_excerpt_zh: 西班牙巴利亚多利德国际电影节（在西班牙被称为 Seminci）于10月23日（周五）开幕，将呈现30场世界首映，并带来汇聚国际影坛最受赞誉的大师以及西班牙新锐电影人的一批片单。展映将持续至10月……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "西班牙巴利亚多利德国际电影节（在西班牙被称为 Seminci）于10月23日（周五）开幕，将呈现30场世界首映，并带来汇聚国际影坛最受赞誉的大师以及西班牙新锐电影人的一批片单。", "links": [{"text": "Valladolid International Film Festival", "url": "https://variety.com/t/valladolid-international-film-festival/"}, {"text": "Seminci", "url": "https://variety.com/t/seminci/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本届电影节迎来第71届，将一直持续到10月31日，共有22部影片入围官方竞赛单元，总计展映208部作品——包括137部长片和71部短片——其中有121部为首映。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "相关报道", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/AmericanDoctor_Still1_CourtesyOfWatermelonPictures-2.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "《美国医生》剧照", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "《美国医生》与《你可以看到一切》领跑电影眼纪录片奖提名", "links": [{"text": "'American Doctor,' 'You Can See Everything' Top Cinema Eye Documentary Nominations", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/awards/american-doctor-you-can-see-everything-cinema-eye-nominations-1236945779/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/TIFFCOM-2026.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "2026年东京国际影视展", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "日本2027年全新动画大奖应让创作者备受瞩目，行业领袖在东京市场表示", "links": [{"text": "Japan’s New 2027 Anime Award Should Put Creators in the Spotlight, Industry Leaders Say at Tokyo Market", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/global/japan-new-2027-anime-award-spotlight-creators-industry-leaders-1236935947/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本届电影节由塑造 Seminci 近年艺术风格的核心团队的两名资深成员掌舵。在前艺术总监何塞·路易斯·西恩富戈斯（José Luis Cienfuegos）于12月逝世后，曾任总协调员的玛丽奥娜·比亚德（Mariona Viader）与曾任节目总监的哈维尔·H·埃斯特拉达（Javier H. Estrada）出任临时联合总监，延续了他在2023年引入的节目策划愿景。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本届入选片单涵盖了截然不同的电影制作方法，从形式实验作品到更具亲和力的独立制作，同时探讨了政治动荡、记忆、流亡与亲密的家庭关系。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“Seminci 的重要之处在于，我们的节目策划能让我们探讨什么是作者电影，”埃斯特拉达说道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "备受赞誉的声音与全新视角", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "角逐巴利亚多利德最高奖项“金穗奖”的影片包括威尼斯金狮奖得主玛丽·埃尔·图赫（May el-Toukhy）的《未知女人》，以及伊尔克·卡塔克（İlker Çatak）的柏林金熊奖得主《黄色信件》。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "paragraph", "text": "“当我们为 Seminci 选片时，我们并不知道《未知女人》会赢得金狮奖，”埃斯特拉达说道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在其他竞赛单元中，阿兰·戈米（Alain Schleinzer）的《罗斯》中，柏林最佳表演奖得主桑德拉·惠勒（Sandra Hüller）饰演了一位在17世纪欧洲女扮男装的女性。兰斯·哈默（Lance Hammer）执导、朱丽叶·比诺什（Juliette Binoche）和汤姆·康特奈（Tom Courtenay）主演的《海中女王》则聚焦复杂多变的家庭关系。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "贝纳尔多·贝托鲁奇（Bernardo Bertolucci）生前参与合写的最后一部剧本，为安德烈亚·帕劳罗（Andrea Pallaoro）执导、艾丽西亚·维坎德（Alicia Vikander）和苏珊·萨兰登（Susan Sarandon）主演的《回音室》提供了基础。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电影节的开幕片和闭幕片进一步巩固了其独特电影声音与国际明星阵容的结合。曾于2020年斩获巴利亚多利德金穗奖的匈牙利导演莉莉·霍瓦特（Lili Horvát）携《火星笔记》回归，该片由麦肯齐·戴维斯（《银翼杀手2049》）主演。加埃尔·加西亚·贝纳尔（Gael García Bernal）则携其第三部导演长片《Hombre al agua》为活动闭幕。", "links": [{"text": "Lili Horvát", "url": "https://variety.com/t/lili-horvat-2/"}, {"text": "Gael García Bernal", "url": "https://variety.com/t/gael-garcia-bernal-2/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "世界首映的重要意义", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管许多国际竞赛单元的影片已在电影节巡回路线上崭露头角，但仍有30部影片——其中略过半数为西班牙制作或合拍片——将在 Seminci 迎来它们的首批观众。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“世界首映对电影人来说总是伴随着某种脆弱性，”埃斯特拉达表示。“如此多的影片选择 Seminci 进行世界首映，这是一份沉甸甸的责任。我们必须呵护每一部电影。但这也同样值得庆祝。观众第一次看到一部电影的时刻是真正激动人心的。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "西班牙入选片单既有成熟的类型片导演，也有首次执导长片的新锐电影人。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "丹尼尔·卡帕尔索罗（Daniel Calparsoro）执导的《El confidente》在官方评选非竞赛单元展映，该片以巴斯克恐怖组织 ETA 的最后几年为背景，由哈维尔·古铁雷斯（Javier Gutiérrez）和米格尔·埃兰（Miguel Herrán）主演，由 Bowfinger 国际影业制作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "同样在非竞赛单元展映的还有大卫·马丁·德·洛斯·桑托斯（David Martín de los Santos）执导的西班牙-秘鲁合拍片《Un hombre en un puente》，该公司有 Vertigo Films 参与。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "家庭关系成为西班牙入选片单中的一个反复出现的主题，尤其是对那些探索家庭纽带、冲突和不断变化的家庭定义的电影人而言。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“重新思考家庭概念是今年 Seminci 的核心主题之一，”埃斯特拉达说道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "演员里卡多·戈麦斯（Ricardo Gómez）的导演处女作《Una familia》在非竞赛单元展映，并在西班牙由 Filmax 发行，该片探讨了塑造父母与子女关系的秘密与未解伤痛。与此同时，伊奥内·埃尔南德斯·萨恩斯（Ione Hernández Sáenz）的长片处女作《Hermanas》由埃len Anaya（埃琳娜·安亚娜）和埃玛·苏亚雷斯（Emma Suárez）主演，将角逐金穗奖，这是一部讲述两姐妹的关系经受家庭危机考验的剧情片。", "links": [{"text": "“Hermanas,”", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/global/sisters-elena-anaya-emma-suarez-ione-hernandez-toronto-1236857177/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "这一主题也延伸至“交汇点”（Meeting Point）竞赛单元，桑德拉·桑切斯（Sandra Sánchez）的《A nadadora》讲述了一名在动荡家庭背景下挣扎的青少年，而莱迪西亚·索拉（Ledicia Sola）的《As augas》则探讨了通过友谊重新定义家庭的可能性。两者都将在巴利亚多利德进行世界首映，同时还有马克·费雷尔（Marc Ferrer）的黑白讽刺喜剧《Cinemanía》，该片此前曾参与 ECAM 论坛的“最后冲刺”（Last Push）环节。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一个发掘之作是克劳迪娅·埃斯特拉达·塔拉斯科（Claudia Estrada Tarascó）的长片处女作《Salen las lobas》，其灵感源于她妹妹在少年司法机构的经历。对于 Oceanika 的制片人阿尔巴·索托拉（Alba Sotorra）而言，其在巴利亚多利德的亮相正值该片的关键时刻。", "links": [{"text": "“Salen las lobas,”", "url": 都是推介克劳迪娅·埃斯特拉达首部电影的战略高地，”索托拉说道。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "除了处女作之外，西班牙电影还通过动画和独立合拍片参与了金穗奖的角逐。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "埃尔温·汉（Ervin Han）与劳尔·加西亚（Raúl García）联合执导的《The Violinist》是一部由新加坡主导、西班牙TV ON Producciones和意大利Altri Occhi联合制作的影片，在通过Wanda Visión于11月13日在西班牙院线上映之前，曾斩获安讷西国际动画电影节最佳长片水晶奖和SACEM音乐奖。", "links": [{"text": "“The Violinist,”", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/festivals/the-violinist-ervin-han-raul-garcia-annecy-cristal-1236797772/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/la-violinista.webp?w=1024", "alt": "", "caption": "《The Violinist》 《The Violinist》 供图：Seminci", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "海伦娜·吉龙（Helena Girón）与塞缪尔·德尔加多（Samuel Delgado）的《Las islas afortunadas》在多伦多电影节举行世界首映后，也入围了金穗奖竞赛单元。Bendita Film Sales负责这部古装剧情片的国际发行，其制片人正与多家发行商洽谈，争取在西班牙院线上映。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Bendita首席执行官路易斯·雷纳特（Luis Renart）表示，电影节入围或许无法直接促成交易，但它能“为有时需要的谈判推波助澜”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "世界首映的范围也延伸到了长片之外。Movistar Plus推出了由豪尔赫和阿尔韦托·桑切斯-卡韦苏多（Jorge and Alberto Sánchez-Cabezudo）兄弟创作、爱德华·费尔南德斯（Eduard Fernández）主演、并与法国Arte电视台联合制作的犯罪惊悚剧《Killing a Bear》（Matar a un oso）的前三集。", "links": [{"text": "“Killing a Bear”", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/tv/global/killing-a-bear-movistar-plus-arte-france-sanchez-cabezudo-1236929739/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "与此同时，由塞尔吉奥·佩里斯-门切塔（Sergio Peris-Mencheta）、玛尔塔·索拉兹（Marta Solaz）和韦罗妮卡·迪亚斯·佩雷斯（Verónica Díaz Pérez）联合执导的El Terrat纪录片《SerYo》，则探讨了佩里斯-门切塔在患病期间的艺术创作。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "共有五位伊朗电影人携作品亮相Seminci展映单元，其中包括阿里·阿斯加里（Ali Asgari）的《A Bit of Light》、佩加·阿汉加拉尼（Pegah Ahangarani）的纪录片《Essays for a Revolution》，以及来自马尼·哈吉吉（Mani Haghighi）、玛莎·卡兰普尔（Mahsa Karampour）和卡里姆·拉克扎德（Karim Lakzadeh）的影片。这些独立入围的作品探讨了战争、镇压、流亡与文化身份。", "links": [{"text": "“Essays for a Revolution”", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/festivals/iranian-pegah-ahangarani-cannes-rehersals-for-a-revolution-1236729598/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "埃斯特拉达表示：“这完全取决于电影本身的品质，最重要的是它们彼此风格迥异。每位电影人都以各自的风格展现了伊朗电影的创作力量。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Seminci对冒险性电影的青睐在“炼金术”（Alchemies）单元中得到了尤为强烈的体现，这是一个于2023年设立、由10部影片组成的竞赛单元，专门展出挑战传统叙事的作品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "其中的亮点包括葡萄牙电影人若昂·佩德罗·罗德里格斯（João Pedro Rodrigues）与若昂·瑞·格拉·达·马塔（João Rui Guerra da Mata）融合了宗教意象与欲望的《13 Pins》；泰德·芬特（Ted Fendt）以柏林为背景的《Foreign Travel》；以及卡里姆·拉克扎德（Karim Lakzadeh）黑色幽默风格的《Living Twice, Dying Thrice》，讲述了矿工伪造死亡以替家人争取赔偿的故事。西班牙入围作品则包括大卫·包特（David Baute）关于一位老人在童年故居中生活的生活特写《Benigno》，以及塞巴斯蒂安·乌里亚（Sebastián Uría）探讨乡村社区消亡的《Adiós, ríos》。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "非竞赛单元“记忆与乌托邦”（Memory & Utopia）通过14部探讨幻想、超现实主义与历史记忆交织的影片，重温了七十年的电影史。亮点包括安娜·马里斯卡尔（Ana Mariscal）1962年佛朗哥时期的间谍惊悚片《Occidente y sabotaje》修复版的世界首映，路易斯·布努埃尔（Luis Buñuel）杰作《一条安达鲁西亚狗》（Un chien andalou）和《黄金时代》（L’Age d’Or）的4K修复版，以及川尻善昭（Yoshiaki Kawajiri）的动画里程碑作品《兽兵卫忍风帖》（Ninja Scroll）。该单元还展出了维拉·希蒂洛娃（Věra Chytilová）、安杰依·瓦伊达（Andrzej Wajda）和伊尔迪科·茵叶蒂（Ildikó Enyedi）的作品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "声音跃居显要位置", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Seminci还为声音在电影中的作用举办了一场大型回顾展。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/willie-jpg-1080x1080-1.webp?w=1024", "alt": "", "caption": "威利·D·伯顿（Willie D. Burton） 供图：Seminci", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "维亚德说：“声音的叙事力量往往居于次要地位，而今年我们希望把它推向最前沿。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该单元从弗里茨·朗（Fritz Lang）的《M》和雅克·塔蒂（Jacques Tati）的《玩乐时间》（Playtime）一直延伸至乔纳森·格雷泽（Jonathan Glazer）的《利益区域》（The Zone of Interest），探讨了电影人如何利用声音传达信息、制造悬念并重塑观众的情感体验。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展映期间还配有与欧洲电影学院声音分会（European Film Academy’s Sound Chapter）合作举办的展览、出版物和专业交流活动。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "除了电影展映之外，Seminci还举办了第六届Merci独立电影市场以及La Meseta实验室，支持独立院线发行和短片开发。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电影节的荣誉奖项授予了巴利亚多利德出生、曾获戈雅奖的女演员埃尔维拉·明格斯（Elvira Mínguez，《Tapas》、《人尽皆知》），以及带来其宣布为最后一部电影的《Behind the Rain》的智利电影人瓦莱里娅·萨尔米恩托（Valeria Sarmiento）。巴塞罗那庞培法布拉大学（Pompeu Fabra University）的纪录片制作大师班项目则荣获学术荣誉金穗奖。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "为了契合电影节对声音的关注，曾八次获得奥斯卡提名并凭借《爵士乐手》（Bird）和《追梦女郎》（Dreamgirls）两度获奖的好莱坞资深电影声音混音师威利·D·伯顿（Willie D. Burton）被授予荣誉金穗奖。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Spain’s Valladolid International Film Festival – known in Spain as Seminci – opens Friday, Oct. 23 with 30 world premieres and a lineup bringing together some of international cinema’s most acclaimed auteurs and an emerging generation of Spanish filmmakers.

Running through Oct. 31, the festival’s 71st edition features 22 films in official competition and 208 titles overall — 137 features and 71 shorts — including 121 premieres.

Related Stories
